g.title: public.providers
g.text: A business or host that sells Services or Experiences. One per login (owner_id is unique). Never deleted: bookings and payouts will point here, so a provider is suspended instead.
The login that owns and manages this provider. A user is a provider exactly when they own a row here. The login cannot be deleted while it owns a provider: suspend or anonymize the provider first.
The business name. Public: shown on the provider's visible listings ("Hosted by ...").
active or suspended. Only admins change it (service role); a suspended provider cannot use provider routes.
The provider's Stripe Connect Express account. Created by the server on first payout setup.
Copied from Stripe: the provider finished the onboarding form. Server-only.
Copied from Stripe: payments can be made to this provider. Server-only.
Copied from Stripe: Stripe can pay out to the provider's bank. Server-only.
The city the provider operates in, picked from active cities. Replaces the old free-text city.
One line about what the provider does. Public on their profile while they can be booked. No contact details.
About the provider, plain text. Public on their profile while they can be booked. No contact details.
The profile photo or logo (square, 512px) in the provider-photos bucket, in the provider's own folder. Public.
The profile photo's 128px copy, for small places. Public.
The cover photo (landscape, at least 1,600 x 600) in the provider-photos bucket, in the provider's own folder. Public.
The public profile's address, /providers/<slug>. Made from the business name when the provider is created; fixed.

g.title: public.cities
g.text: The markets lokl operates in, each named after its main city and covering its metro area (Atlanta covers Decatur, Marietta and so on). Admin-managed. Never deleted: providers and listings point here, so a market is deactivated instead.
Two-letter US state code, e.g. GA.
The market's time zone, a real IANA name (America/New_York): every booking, session and listing time in this market is shown in it. Required; checked against the database's zone names.
Inactive cities are hidden everywhere public and in the provider city picker.
Display order in lists and pickers, lowest first.

g.title: public.providers:city_id->public.cities:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (city_id) REFERENCES cities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.service_areas
g.text: Areas within a market: neighborhoods, cities or towns, and zip codes. Where "I come to you" Services travel, and the public location label on listings. Admin-managed. Never deleted: listings will point here, so an area is deactivated instead.
The market this area belongs to.
neighborhood (e.g. Old Fourth Ward), city (a city or town within the market, e.g. Decatur) or zip (a five-digit zip code).
Shown to customers, e.g. Old Fourth Ward, Decatur or 30312. Unique per market and kind.
Inactive areas are hidden everywhere public.

g.title: public.service_areas:city_id->public.cities:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (city_id) REFERENCES cities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.categories
g.text: Service and Experience categories. Flat and admin-managed; each listing belongs to one category of its own kind. Never deleted: listings will point here, so a category is deactivated instead.
service or experience. A listing can only use a category of its own kind.
Shown to customers, e.g. Hair and beauty. 2 to 60 characters.
URL-safe identifier, unique within its kind, e.g. hair-and-beauty.
Optional. Shown on the category page later. Up to 500 characters.
Inactive categories are hidden everywhere public, and so are their listings.
Display order within its kind, lowest first.

g.title: public.listings
g.text: A Service or Experience a provider offers. Deleted only while it has never been live (published_at is null); after that it is unlisted or unpublished, never deleted, because bookings will point at it.
service or experience. Fixed at creation.
A category of the same kind, enforced by the (category_id, kind) reference.
Generated from the title with a short random suffix when the listing is created. Used by public listing pages; not changed afterwards.
Whole price in cents for a Service; per person for an Experience.
Required for Experiences; optional for Services.
Services only: provider_location (customer comes to the provider) or customer_location (provider travels, within listing_service_areas). Null for Experiences.
The public location label, e.g. Old Fourth Ward. Required for provider-location Services and Experiences. Must be in the listing's city.
draft, submitted, live, rejected or unpublished. Changed only by server routes.
Why an Experience was sent back. Set on rejection; cleared on resubmission.
Set the first time the listing goes live and never cleared.
Why the owner took the listing down, 10 to 1,000 characters; shown to the provider. Set when unpublished; cleared on restore. Server-only.

Services: instant (booked and paid from a slot) or approve (a slot requested, the card held, the provider accepts or declines). Required on every Service, chosen by the provider (no default); can change while live (bookings keep the mode they were made under). Null on Experiences.
Services: free time after each booking (for travel), 0 to 120 minutes; null uses the provider's default.

g.title: public.listings:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.listings:city_id->public.cities:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (city_id) REFERENCES cities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.listings:area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.listings:category_id->public.categories:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (category_id, kind) REFERENCES categories(id, kind) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.listing_addresses
g.text: A listing's exact address. Private: readable only by the listing's provider and the admin (customers with a confirmed booking come later). Required for provider-location Services and Experiences before publishing or submitting. Deleted with its listing, or by the provider when it is no longer needed.
Optional arrival notes, e.g. "Side entrance, ring twice".

g.title: public.listing_addresses:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.listing_service_areas
g.text: Where an "I come to you" Service travels. At least one row is required before a customer-location Service can go live. Rows go with their listing; the provider removes a row to stop covering an area.

g.title: public.listing_service_areas:service_area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (service_area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.listing_service_areas:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.listing_photos
g.text: Photos of a listing, at most 8. Position 0 is the cover. At least one is required before a listing is published or submitted. Removed by the provider (not while submitted or unpublished, and never the last one of a live listing) or by the admin; rows go with their listing. Removing a row leaves the stored file.
Path in the listing-photos bucket: <provider_id>/<listing_id>/<random uuid>.<ext>. Must be in this listing's own folder.
0 to 7, unique per listing. 0 is the cover photo.
Describes the photo for screen reader users. Required, 5 to 200 characters.

The card-sized copy (about 600px wide) of this photo, in the same folder: <uuid>.card.webp for <uuid>.<ext>, or <uuid>.card.jpg where the browser couldn't encode WebP. Null for photos added before card copies existed; pages then use the full photo. Set on upload, never changed.

g.title: public.listing_photos:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.experience_sessions
g.text: Dated sessions of an Experience, each with a number of spots. Providers add and change future sessions (not while the listing is submitted or unpublished); a session that has started is kept as it is. Deleted with their listing, or by the provider before they start; once bookings exist, a session with bookings is cancelled instead.
When the session starts. Entered and shown in the listing city's time zone (cities.timezone). Must be in the future and at most a year ahead when a provider adds or moves it.
Spots in the session, 1 to 500. Spots left will be worked out from bookings.
scheduled or cancelled. A cancelled session can't be changed or scheduled again.

g.title: public.experience_sessions:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.notifications
g.text: Things that happened to a provider's listings because of an admin action. Written only by the listings_notify_status_change trigger. Providers read their own and mark them read. Deleted with their listing; otherwise kept (a cleanup of old read ones comes later).
The recipient: the business that owns the listing.

listing_approved (submitted -> live), listing_rejected (submitted -> rejected), listing_unpublished (live -> unpublished) or listing_restored (unpublished -> live). The sentence shown is built from this and the listing's current title.
When the provider marked it read; null while unread. Once set it doesn't change, and it can't be cleared.
For booking notifications: the booking it's about.
The report lokl replied to (kind support_reply).

g.title: public.notifications:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.notifications:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.bookings
g.text: A customer's booking of a Service (a request the provider accepts) or an Experience session (paid at once). Written only by the website's server. lokl holds the payment and transfers the provider's share 24 hours after the booking ends. Never deleted: payments, refunds and payouts point here.

pending_payment (in Stripe Checkout; spots held until reserved_until) -> requested (Service: card on hold, waiting for the provider) -> confirmed (accepted and charged, or Experience paid) -> completed (it happened) -> paid_out (provider's share transferred). Or declined, expired, cancelled. A customer's late cancellation (no refund) can still be paid out. The allowed changes are enforced by bookings_guard.
Experiences: the session's start, copied. Services: the accepted preferred time.
starts_at plus the listing's duration (or starts_at if it has none). Set by the database.
People booked: 1 for Services; 1 to 10 for Experiences, and no more than the spots left.
The customer's name from checkout. The provider sees it on the request.
When the provider's share may be transferred: 24 hours after ends_at. Set by the database on confirmation.
Set when the customer reports the provider didn't show; holds the payout until the admin acts.
Who made the latest status change; copied into booking_events.
"I come to you" Services: the customer's city, copied from their address when the request is made, so the provider sees roughly where before accepting. Never changes.
"I come to you" Services: the customer's zip code, copied like customer_city. The street address stays in booking_addresses until the provider accepts.
How lokl resolved a no-show report: paid_provider (the payout goes ahead) or refunded (the booking was cancelled with a full refund).

The booking page's key for the checkout attempt that made this booking: a retry with the same key returns this booking instead of a second one. Unique per customer. Written only by the booking functions (the server).
SHA-256 of the attempt's details (the validated request), so the same key with other details is refused. Written only by the booking functions.
Services booked from a slot: the listing's booking mode when it was made (instant or approve). Null for Experiences and old requests. Written only by create_service_booking.

g.title: public.notifications:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_reports
g.text: A problem a provider reported to lokl. Never deleted, and its details never change: only its status moves (on the admin's board, by a reply, or by the provider's "This is sorted"), with the columns its triggers keep.
A Safety report: first on the board, emailed to every admin at once, and only an admin closes it.
The earlier report this follows on from: a reply to one resolved over 30 days ago starts a new report.
todo, in_progress, waiting (on the provider), done. Providers see Received, We're looking into it, Waiting for your reply, Resolved.
When it last moved to Done: a reply within 30 days of it reopens the report.

g.title: public.notifications:support_report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (support_report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.commission_rates
g.text: lokl's commission per kind of listing, in basis points (1200 = 12%). Public (the Fees page). Admin-editable. Each booking copies the rate in force when it's created, so changes never touch past bookings. Never deleted.
Commission in basis points, 0 to 5000 (0% to 50%).

g.title: public.bookings:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.bookings:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.bookings:session_id->public.experience_sessions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES experience_sessions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_events
g.text: Every status change of a booking: from, to, who (customer, provider, admin, system, stripe) and when. Written by a trigger. Never changed or deleted.

g.title: public.booking_events:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_contacts
g.text: The customer's email and optional phone for a booking. The provider reads them only once the booking is accepted or confirmed. Never deleted.

g.title: public.booking_contacts:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_addresses
g.text: Where an "I come to you" Service takes place: the customer's address. The provider reads it only once the booking is accepted. Never deleted.

g.title: public.booking_addresses:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_emails
g.text: Booking emails to send and what happened to each (the outbox and the log). Filled by triggers on bookings; sent by the website's server. Server only; admins can read. Never deleted.
Which email: customer_* go to the customer, provider_* to the provider (docs/design/booking-and-checkout.md, Emails).
customer or provider, from the kind.
When the sender may try a pending email (later after each failure).
Where it was sent, recorded when sent (or skipped).

g.title: public.booking_emails:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_actions
g.text: Every admin action on bookings, emails, providers, reviews and problem reports: who, what, when and why. Written by the website's admin routes with the service role; read by admins. Never deleted.
For suspending or reinstating a provider: the optional message lokl added to the provider's email. (The reason is internal and never sent.)
For review moderation: the written review rule the removal applied.
The request this action answered: approved (the action ran, as the owner) or done by the owner directly. With admin_requests.requested_by, the history names who asked and who approved.

g.title: public.admin_requests
g.text: Support's requests for what only the owner may do (admin roles, step 5b): a refund over the limit, releasing a payout hold, resolving a report by paying the provider, suspending or reinstating a provider. Pending until the owner approves (the action runs, as the owner, and closes it), declines (with a note) or acts directly ("done by the owner"), the asker withdraws it, or 7 days pass (expired). One pending request per thing. Never deleted; only its decision is ever written, once.
A refund's amount when asked: what was left of the charge then. Approving refunds what's left at that moment, which the approval screen shows if it changed.
The payout hold to release, as it was when asked.
What approving (or the owner's own action) did, in a few words.

g.title: public.admin_actions:request_id->public.admin_requests:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (request_id) REFERENCES admin_requests(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.commission_rate_changes
g.text: Each change to a commission rate: from, to, who and when. Filled by a trigger on commission_rates; read by admins. Never deleted.

g.title: public.job_runs
g.text: Each timed job run (website /api/jobs/*): how many bookings it looked at, changed and couldn't handle, with the failures. Written by the website's server; read by admins.
True when a batch was full, so more rows may be waiting for the next run. Written by the job route.

g.title: public.provider_emails
g.text: Emails about a provider's account (paused, active again) to send, and what happened to each. One per admin action. Queued by admin_set_provider_status(); sent by the website's server. Server only; admins can read. Never deleted.
lokl's optional message, included in the email only if written.
For provider_profile_edited: which parts of the profile lokl removed.
For provider_profile_edited: the profile rule they broke (PROFILE_RULES in packages/types).

g.title: public.provider_emails:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.provider_emails:admin_action_id->public.admin_actions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (admin_action_id) REFERENCES admin_actions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_finances
g.text: A booking's money side: the commission split (copied at booking), payout holds and failures, Stripe ids, dispute and reversal details. Read by the booking's provider and admins, never the customer; written by the server. Never deleted.
Why this booking's payout is held for lokl to review (see the pay-out job). Set by the job; cleared only by the admin.
Stripe ids are readable by the booking's provider, though no page shows them (a possible later refinement: docs/design/booking-and-checkout.md).

Payout hold reasons an admin has released for this booking (release-payout). The pay-out job doesn't hold the payout again for a released judgement (a lost dispute, a refund, a suspended provider); an open dispute and a reported problem always hold, and a fresh refusal from Stripe holds again. Only grows.

g.title: public.booking_finances:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.booking_reports
g.text: The customer's "the provider didn't show up" note. Read by that customer and admins, never the provider; written by the server; final once written. Never deleted.

g.title: public.booking_reports:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides
g.text: Destination guides: articles about a place or theme in a market that recommend live lokl listings. Admin-written. Draft columns are edited; live columns (title, teaser, body, cover_photo_id) are set only by publish_guide(). Visitors see published guides through the website's server. Unpublished, never deleted, once published.
The draft body as Editor.js blocks (JSON). Rendered by lokl's own renderer, never as raw HTML.
Up to 160 characters: shown under the photo on cards and the homepage, and used as the meta description.
The live listings block's area (with category_id and listing_kind): copied from the draft_ columns by publish_guide(), like the text and cover.
True from the moment an AI draft lands in the draft until the admin confirms they've checked the highlighted phrases and the facts. Publishing is refused while true.
When the live text or cover last changed: "Last updated" on the page and dateModified in structured data.

g.title: public.guides:market_id->public.cities:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (market_id) REFERENCES cities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides:area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides:draft_area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (draft_area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides:category_id->public.categories:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides:draft_category_id->public.categories:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (draft_category_id) REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guide_photos
g.text: Photos of a guide, in the public guide-photos bucket under <guide id>/: resized in the browser (longest side at most 2,400px, metadata removed), with a ~600px card copy. Credits as the licence asks: none for own photos; "Photo by {name} on Unsplash" with links; or the credit, licence and source for another licence (commercial use confirmed).

g.title: public.guides:cover_photo_id->public.guide_photos:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (cover_photo_id) REFERENCES guide_photos(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guides:draft_cover_photo_id->public.guide_photos:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (draft_cover_photo_id) REFERENCES guide_photos(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_photos:guide_id->public.guides:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (guide_id) REFERENCES guides(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.guide_versions
g.text: A snapshot of a guide's live copy each time it's published, with who and when. Written by publish_guide(); read by admins.

g.title: public.guide_versions:area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_versions:category_id->public.categories:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_versions:guide_id->public.guides:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (guide_id) REFERENCES guides(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.guide_versions:cover_photo_id->public.guide_photos:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (cover_photo_id) REFERENCES guide_photos(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_ai_drafts
g.text: Every AI draft request: what was sent (topic, area, category, the admin's notes), the model, the reply or error, tokens and cost, who and when. Written by the admin app's server; read by admins. Kept if its guide is deleted (the cost log).
The guide's draft just before this AI draft replaced it: title, teaser, body, area, category, kind and its review state. Null if the draft didn't land.
When the admin put the previous draft back. Set once; the previous draft can be restored only while this is the guide's latest AI draft.

g.title: public.guide_ai_drafts:area_id->public.service_areas:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (area_id) REFERENCES service_areas(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_ai_drafts:category_id->public.categories:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.guide_ai_drafts:guide_id->public.guides:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (guide_id) REFERENCES guides(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

g.title: public.homepage_features
g.text: The guides on the homepage: position 1 is the main guide (the hero), 2 and 3 the guides section's cards. Chosen by the admin; only published guides. Unpublishing or deleting a guide removes it; without a main guide, the cards aren't shown.
1 is the main guide (the hero); 2 and 3 are the guides section's two cards.

g.title: public.homepage_features:guide_id->public.guides:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (guide_id) REFERENCES guides(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.saved_listings
g.text: Listings a customer saved (their "Saved" list). Private to that customer: nobody else can read it, not even the listing's provider or admins. Deleted with the customer's login or the listing.

g.title: public.saved_listings:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.saved_providers
g.text: Providers a customer saved (their "Saved" list). Private to that customer: nobody else can read it, not even the provider or admins. Deleted with the customer's login; providers are never deleted.

g.title: public.saved_providers:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.reviews
g.text: A customer's review of a completed booking: one to five stars and their words, public at once. One per booking. Deleted only by its customer within 14 days of the booking's end; removed (status) only by an admin, under the written rules.

g.title: public.reviews:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.reviews:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.reviews:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.review_replies
g.text: The provider's one public reply to a review. Editable and deletable by them at any time (deleting is also how a removed reply is written again); removed (status) only by an admin. Goes with its review.

g.title: public.review_replies:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.review_replies:review_id->public.reviews:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (review_id) REFERENCES reviews(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.review_reports
g.text: A signed-in person's report that a review or its reply breaks a written rule, for the admin's queue. One per person per review and target. Goes with its review (or the reporter's login).

g.title: public.review_reports:review_id->public.reviews:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (review_id) REFERENCES reviews(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.listing_ratings
g.text: Each listing's published reviews: count, star total and average (rounded half up to one decimal). Kept by the reviews_recount trigger; never written from the apps.
Published reviews with 5 stars (stars_1 to stars_4 likewise). Kept by recount_ratings.

g.title: public.listing_ratings:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_ratings
g.text: Each provider's published reviews across all their listings (including ones no longer live): count, star total and average. Kept by the reviews_recount trigger.
Published reviews with 5 stars (stars_1 to stars_4 likewise). Kept by recount_ratings.

g.title: public.provider_ratings:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_schedules
g.text: A provider's booking settings, one row per provider (defaults apply without one). The provider writes it; deleting it goes back to the defaults. Goes with its provider (providers are never deleted).
How far ahead customers can book, in days (7 to 180).
The least notice a booking needs, in minutes (one hour to one week).
How often a slot can start: every 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
Free time after each booking (for travel), for Services without their own and for Experience sessions.

g.title: public.provider_schedules:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_weekly_hours
g.text: A provider's repeating weekly hours: one row per interval (a day can have several). Wall-clock times in the market's time zone. The provider adds, changes and deletes them freely; nothing points here.
The end of the interval, after starts; 24:00 is the end of the day.

g.title: public.provider_weekly_hours:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_date_hours
g.text: Hours for one date, replacing that weekday's weekly hours: one row per interval. A day off is time off for that date. The provider adds, changes and deletes them freely; nothing points here.

g.title: public.provider_date_hours:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_time_off
g.text: Whole days a provider isn't available, from starts_on to ends_on (inclusive), whatever their hours. The provider adds, changes and deletes them freely; nothing points here.
For the provider alone (customers never see it).

g.title: public.provider_time_off:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_holds
g.text: The provider's time each Service booking (from a slot) and each scheduled Experience session takes: [start, end + buffer). No two of a provider's holds overlap, across all their listings. Written only by triggers on bookings and experience_sessions; deleted when the booking is released (expired, declined, cancelled) or the session cancelled or deleted. Not readable through the API.
The time held: from the start to the end plus the buffer, as it was when the booking or session was made.

g.title: public.provider_holds:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_holds:session_id->public.experience_sessions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES experience_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.provider_holds:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: private.booking_records
g.text: A booking with its finances and no-show note, for the website's server only (service role). Updatable: one statement writes booking_finances, booking_reports and bookings, in that order, so the booking's rules see the money.

g.title: public.service_open_days
g.text: Each market day a Service has a bookable time, with its start times (and the first and last of them), as of its last refresh (service_open_days_refreshed). Worked out by the slot core; only refresh_service_open_days writes it. Search reads it through service_open_matches. Derived data: rewritten freely, and deleted with its listing.
The day's last bookable time when refreshed. Search checks it against now plus the notice, so a day whose times have all come within the notice no longer matches.
The day's bookable start times when refreshed, in order (first_at is the first, last_at the last). Search takes the earliest at or after now plus the notice, the time the panel would show.

g.title: public.service_open_days:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_open_days_refreshed
g.text: When each Service's open days were last worked out, how far ahead they cover, and its notice then (search checks times against now plus it). Derived data: rewritten freely, and deleted with its listing.

g.title: public.service_open_days_refreshed:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_open_days_refreshed:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_open_days_pending
g.text: Providers whose open days a transaction changed, refreshed (and the rows deleted) when it commits. Empty between transactions; derived data.
The provider to refresh at commit. No foreign key: a provider deleted in the same transaction (its holds and hours going with it) is noted too, and simply has nothing to refresh.

g.title: public.support_reports:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_reports:listing_id->public.listings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_reports:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_reports:follows_report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (follows_report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_messages
g.text: A report's thread: messages from the provider and from lokl. Permanent: never edited or deleted (append_only_guard). The provider reads their own reports' messages; admins read all. Never published to Realtime, and never in an email.

g.title: public.support_messages:report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_notes
g.text: Admins' private notes on a report: the provider never sees them. Permanent (append_only_guard). Written by the server for an admin.

g.title: public.support_notes:report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_report_events
g.text: Each status a report moved to, who moved it and when (from_status null: sent). Written only by a trigger; append-only.

g.title: public.support_report_events:report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_notifications
g.text: The admin bell: a new report (support_safety for a Safety one) or a provider's reply, one row per admin login; and a team change (team_change, its admin_actions row) for every active owner. Each admin reads and marks read only their own. Ids only: published to Realtime, so an open report reloads its thread. Deleted with the admin's login.
For a team change: the admin_actions row saying who did what (invite, role change, removal, second factor reset, join).
For a request: the request (request_new to each owner; request_decided to the person who asked).

g.title: public.admin_notifications:admin_action_id->public.admin_actions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (admin_action_id) REFERENCES admin_actions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_notifications:report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_notifications:admin_request_id->public.admin_requests:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (admin_request_id) REFERENCES admin_requests(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_emails
g.text: The problem reports' email outbox: lokl's reply to the provider, and a new report (urgent for Safety) or a reply to each admin. Never the message text. Only its delivery details change (outbox_guard); never deleted.

g.title: public.support_emails:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.support_emails:report_id->public.support_reports:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (report_id) REFERENCES support_reports(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_members
g.text: Who may use lokl's admin, and as what: owner (everything) or support. Read live on every request (admin_role()). Never deleted: a removal is a status, so the history stays; at least one active owner, always. Written only by the server and the team functions (owner only), never directly by a signed-in user.
invited (asked, not yet joined: no access), active (access, after passing the second factor), removed (no access).

g.title: public.public_content_versions
g.text: One number per scope of public content (listings, markets, guides), raised by triggers whenever that content changes. The website's cached public routes include the numbers in their cache keys, so a change shows at once. Three fixed rows, never deleted; only the triggers write them.
Raised by one for every statement that changes this scope's content.

g.title: public.admin_emails
g.text: The team's email outbox (admin roles, 2026-10-19): an invitation to the person invited (admin_invite), and each team change to every active owner (admin_team_change), their own included. Never a reason or note. Only its delivery details change (outbox_guard); never deleted. The server sends it; the owner reads it.

g.title: public.admin_emails:admin_action_id->public.admin_actions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (admin_action_id) REFERENCES admin_actions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_settings
g.text: The owner's settings for the team (admin roles): one row (id is always true). Support refunds directly up to refund_limit_cents of what's left of a charge; above it, they ask the owner (admin_requests). Never deleted. Changed by the owner from the Settings page (step 5d); until then, by migration.
The most support can refund directly, in cents, measured on what's left of the charge (default $150).

g.title: public.admin_requests:provider_id->public.providers:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES providers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.admin_requests:booking_id->public.bookings:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (booking_id) REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
